title: Independence in Rotational Differential-Linear Correlation Evaluation
summary: Rotational differential-linear correlation evaluation relies on independence assumptions; whether they can be weakened or removed to explain experimental distinguishers remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the independence assumptions used in evaluating rotational differential-linear correlations can be weakened or eliminated, potentially enabling the correlation-evaluation method to explain experimental distinguishers that remain unexplained.

scope.domain: Rotational differential-linear cryptanalysis of ARX ciphers.
assumptions: Mutual independence of the bit-mismatch events used by the rotational differential-linear correlation-evaluation method.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the independence assumptions can be weakened or eliminated, potentially allowing the method to explain currently unexplained experimental distinguishers.

citations.label: Rotational Differential-Linear Distinguishers of ARX Ciphers with Arbitrary Output Linear Masks

progress.summary: The paper explicitly asks whether its correlation-evaluation method can avoid or weaken its independence assumptions and suggests that resolving this issue may explain experimental distinguishers that remain unexplained.
citation_labels: Zhongfeng Niu et al., Rotational Differential-Linear Distinguishers of ARX Ciphers with Arbitrary Output Linear Masks
